title: What If the Earth Stopped Spinning?
lines: What if the Earth suddenly stopped spinning?
At the equator, | you're moving at {about/~about} {1,670 kilometers an hour~one thousand six hundred seventy kilometers an hour}.
You don't feel {it,/~it,} because {everything/~everything} moves with you.
Stop the planet suddenly, | and {anything/~anything} not bolted {down/~down} keeps going east, at that speed.
So does the air: winds of more {than/~than} {1,000 kilometers an hour~a thousand kilometers an hour}.
Over time, the {oceans/~oceans} would start to move.
Spinning makes Earth bulge about {21 kilometers~twenty-one kilometers} at the equator.
Without it, that water slides toward the poles.
{2~Two} polar oceans, and one giant {continent/~continent} wrapped around the middle.
And one day would last a whole year: | {6 months~six months} of daylight, {6 months~six months} of night.
The strange part? | Earth really is slowing {down./~down.}
About {400 million years~four hundred million years} ago, | a year had roughly {400 days~four hundred days}.
Fossil corals recorded it, | in their daily growth {rings./~rings.}
At today's rate, how long until a day lasts {25 hours~twenty-five hours}? | About {20,000~twenty thousand} years, | or about {200 million~two hundred million} years? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: If the Earth stopped spinning, | the winds would blow at more than {1,000 kilometers an hour~a thousand kilometers an hour}.
